title.narrative: Interamerican special rapporteur for freedom of expression, 2024- 2026

description.narrative:
Den Interamerikanska specialrapportören för yttrandefrihet (RFOE), tillhörande den Interamerikanska kommissionen för mänskliga rättigheter (IACHR) under Organisationen för de Amerikanska Staterna (OAS), är det regionala expertorganet med mandat att främja och granska situationen i förhållande till yttrandefrihet, ge expertråd till IACHR angående skydd och åtgärder, samt ta fall till den Interamerikanska domstolen för mänskliga rättigheter (I/A court for H.R.) för främjande och skydd av yttrandefrihet.
Insatsen syftar till att garantera rätten till yttrandefrihet som ett sätt att stärka och upprätthålla demokratiska institutioner och rättsstatens principer i Latinamerika. Detta kommer att göras genom att arbeta mot följande fem mål i enlighet med RFOEs arbetsplan 2023 - 2025:
1. Arbetsflöden och processer för RFOEs kontor upprättas och systematiseras.
2. Expertråd ges till den Interamerikanska kommissionen för mänskliga rättigheter avseende framställningar, ärenden, försktighetsåtgärder och provisoriska åtgärder.
3. Situationen för yttrandefrihet i regionen följs upp.
4. Interamerikanska normer för yttrandefrihet främjas.
5. Expertkunskaper om yttrandefrihet delas och publiceras.

The Office of the Special Rapporteur for Freedom of Expression (RFOE) of the Inter-American Commission for Human Rights (IACHR) under the Organisation of American States (OAS) is the regional expert entity in the region with the mandate to promote and monitor the situation in relation to freedom of expression, provide expert advice to the IACHR regarding precautionary measures and petitions to the Inter-American Court of Human Rights related to the protection of freedom of expression.
The intervention aims at guaranteeing the right to freedom of expression for the strengthening and preservation of democratic institutions and the rule of law in Latin America, this will be done by working towards the following five objectives in accordance with RFOE work plan 2023 - 2025:
1. Work flows and processes of the Office of the RFOE are established and systematized.
2. The IACHR receives expert advice from RFOE for the evaluation of petitions, cases, precautionary, and provisional measures.
3. The situation of freedom of expression in the hemisphere is monitored in a timely manner.
4. Inter-American standards of freedom of expression are widely promoted.
5. Expert knowledge on freedom of expression in produced and published.

sector.narrative: Media and free flow of information

description.narrative:
The activity period for the contribution began in August 2024. According to the first report submitted to Sida by the Special Rapporteur for Freedom of Expression (SRFoE), progress has been made across the four agreed results:
Under Result 1, which focuses on establishing and systematizing the workflows and processes of the SRFoE Office, administrative and operational improvements were achieved. These include the updating of the offices organogram and job descriptions, as well as the development of a matrix for registering monitoring information. Additionally, procedures were enhanced and streamlined for following up on the mechanism of petitions and cases, monitoring requests for precautionary measures, and organizing listening sessions.
In relation to Result 2, which aims to provide expert advice to the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights (IACHR), the SRFoE reviewed 24 requests for precautionary measures to support the protection of freedom of expression. Of these, five were granted by the IACHR, including three that directly benefited Venezuelan journalists. The SRFoE also drafted a merits report in a case against Venezuela before the Inter-American Court of Human Rights, contributing to the development of jurisprudence on strategic lawsuits against public participation (SLAPP). Furthermore, three admissibility reports prepared by the SRFoEconcerning cases in Panama, Peru, and Brazilwere approved by the IACHR.
Progress under Result 3, which concerns timely monitoring of the situation of freedom of expression in the hemisphere, was also notable. The SRFoE conducted ten listening sessions to gather information from civil society, journalists, and media professionals in countries such as Bolivia, Colombia, Cuba, Ecuador, Mexico, and Peru. In addition, official letters were submitted to nine States requesting information on issues of particular concern regarding the protection of the right to freedom of expression. The Office also issued six press releases and four joint statements with the IACHR to raise awareness and call for action from States in response to critical cases in the region.
For Result 4, which focuses on the promotion of Inter-American standards on freedom of expression, the SRFoE participated in sixteen events, five of which addressed the intersection of freedom of expression with internet governance and artificial intelligence. The Office also produced four podcast episodes exploring jurisprudence from the Inter-American system in cases related to freedom of expression.
Under Result 5, which involves the production and dissemination of expert knowledge, the SRFoE provided technical assistance to the Government of Colombia. This support led to the signing of the Presidential Directive on Freedom of Expression, which establishes guidelines to align national practices with international standards. The directive, signed by the President of Colombia, in the presence of the SRFoE and the Swedish Ambassador, is the first of its kind in the Americas and sets a precedent for preventing stigmatization and promoting respectful engagement between public officials and the press. The SRFoE also supported the Government of Ecuador in strengthening its mechanisms and policies for the protection of journalists at risk. Additionally, a joint statement with other international rapporteurs and organizations was issued on the protection of freedom of association, addressing the growing global concern of foreign agents and influence laws that restrict the autonomy and operations of civil society organizations.
Finally, under Result 6, which addresses the protection of journalists and other actors amid escalating violence in Venezuelas post-electoral context, the SRFoE collected testimonies and conducted hearing sessions on human rights abuses following the 2024 electoral process. These efforts have led to the production of thematic reports, press releases, and recommendations. A comprehensive account of the outcomes under this result will be provided in the final report for the special task outlined in Amendment No. 2, scheduled for submission in June 2025.
